items.headline: RBI conducts VRRR auction, eases FPI KYC rules; analysts anticipate two rate hikes by Dec 2026
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is conducting an overnight variable rate reverse repo (VRRR) auction worth ₹1 lakh crore to absorb excess liquidity and earlier eased Know Your Customer (KYC) rules for Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs). Analysts expect two rate hikes, totaling 50 basis points, by December 2026 due to global tightening, excess liquidity, and inflation concerns. India's retail inflation rose to 4.82% in August 2026, with September expected near 5%. Moody's raised India's FY27 growth forecast to 7%.

items.headline: Indian markets open amidst mixed global cues; oil prices ease but Middle East tensions persist
items.summary: Indian markets are opening amidst mixed global cues. Asian markets are trading mixed to higher, with South Korea's Kospi rising 0.85% and the Kosdaq gaining 0.43%, while Australia's S&P/ASX 200 declined 0.49%. Japanese markets are closed. Global sentiment is influenced by renewed tensions in the Middle East, though crude oil prices eased, with Brent crude futures falling 2.10% to $101.69 a barrel and US crude down 1.93% at $98.36 a barrel. Elevated oil prices and the 10-year US Treasury yield near 5% remain concerns. US stock futures edged higher, and investors await a meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

items.headline: Indian benchmarks open green; Capital goods, healthcare, oil & gas, banking lead gains; IT, pharma stocks show positive outlook
items.summary: The Indian equity benchmark indices, Sensex and Nifty, started the day in the green, with Sensex up 0.32% and Nifty up 16.20 points. Capital goods, healthcare, oil & gas, and banking stocks led the gains, while IT, consumer durables, and FMCG lagged. IT stocks showed a positive outlook after Accenture raised its FY25 guidance, with Infosys and Wipro ADRs gaining 3%. Pharma stocks continued to rally due to USFDA approvals and a favorable USDINR exchange rate. Mid-cap and small-cap segments are expected to show momentum, and sugar stocks are expected to gain from government plans to allow exports.
